topic.label: Environmental Systems Engineering
topic.desc: Environmental Systems Engineering: designing and analysing the water, air, waste and energy systems that link human activity to natural environments.

concepts: Quantifying how precipitation, runoff, groundwater and storage move through watersheds, and sizing infrastructure that manages flood and supply.
Design of physical, chemical and biological processes that remove contaminants from drinking water and wastewater to meet discharge and potability standards.
Characterising emission sources, atmospheric dispersion and control technologies for particulates and gaseous pollutants.
Planning collection, recycling, composting, landfilling and hazardous waste handling as an integrated materials system.
Evaluating the cradle-to-grave resource use and environmental impact of products and infrastructure to compare design alternatives.
Linking contaminant fate, exposure and health risk to the regulatory framework and spatial data that govern environmental decisions.
skills: Converts design storms into runoff hydrographs with curve-number or unit-hydrograph methods and checks peak flow and volume against a mass balance.
Solves Darcy flow toward wells and drains for given aquifer properties and checks drawdown against the Theis or Thiem solution.
Runs sequent-peak storage analysis on an inflow record to find firm yield and checks that storage never goes negative over the record.
Sizes coagulation, sedimentation, filtration and disinfection units from flow and loading criteria and checks detention times and overflow rates against design ranges.
Computes aeration volume, sludge age and oxygen demand from influent BOD and nitrogen loads and checks the result with a steady-state biomass balance.
Applies the Streeter-Phelps model below an effluent outfall and checks the critical dissolved oxygen deficit against the stream standard.
Estimates ground-level pollutant concentrations downwind of a stack using stability-class dispersion coefficients and checks maxima against ambient standards.
Compiles source emission rates from activity data and emission factors and checks totals by reconciling against reported facility data.
Matches cyclones, baghouses, electrostatic precipitators or scrubbers to a gas stream and checks the required removal efficiency is met.
Computes landfill airspace, liner requirements and leachate generation with a water balance and checks capacity against projected waste tonnage.
Builds a composition profile of a municipal waste stream from sorting data and checks that fractions sum to the measured total mass.
Maps recovery, reuse and disposal pathways for a material and checks the flow diagram for mass conservation at every node.
Assembles material and energy flows per functional unit for each life cycle stage and checks completeness against the declared system boundary.
Converts inventory flows to carbon dioxide equivalents with stated characterisation factors and checks the arithmetic by recomputing per stage.
Ranks engineering alternatives on cost, energy and impact criteria with weighted scoring and checks that the ranking holds under sensitivity analysis.
Calculates chronic daily intake and hazard quotients or cancer risk for an exposure pathway and checks inputs against standard exposure factors.
Solves advection-dispersion with decay for a plume and checks the analytic result against a numerical solution in Wolfram.
Maps facilities, receptors and permit limits in a GIS layer and checks each monitored value against its regulatory limit.
